program_name: Physics (Fisica) - Master of Science / Laurea Magistrale in Fisica
teaching_language: Fully English. The programme is taught entirely in English; the official language of the course is English and no Italian-language track (percorso) is offered for this degree. Knowledge of English at CEFR B2 or higher is an admission requirement for every applicant (EU and non-EU alike).
campus: Trento - Povo campus (Department of Physics, Ferrari 1 Building, Via Sommarive 5, 38123 Povo, Trento TN)
admission_type: Restricted / selective admission based on evaluation of qualifications and, where required, an oral interview. There is no TOLC and no numero programmato national test. Two separate procedures exist: (1) EU citizens and equivalents (plus non-EU citizens already legally residing in Italy) apply through the departmental admission call with rolling application sessions; admission is granted once curricular requirements are met, with an interview to verify personal preparation unless the applicant qualifies for exemption. (2) Non-EU citizens living outside Italy apply through a separate public selection call ('public selection based on qualifications and, if appropriate, interview') with a fixed quota of places and a single early deadline.
academic_requirements: Degree requirement: a Bachelor's degree (or equivalent university qualification) of at least three years, in Physics or a Physics-related field, awarded by an internationally recognised university; foreign qualifications must be recognised as suitable. Curricular requirements: at least 84 ECTS in Mathematics and Physics scientific-disciplinary fields combined (MAT/* + FIS/*), of which at least 24 ECTS in the Mathematics area (MAT/*) and at least 54 ECTS in the Physics area (FIS/*). Personal preparation: verified by an interview with a committee appointed annually by the Department of Physics. Interview exemption: applicants who have earned at least 30 ECTS in MAT/* fields and at least 90 ECTS in FIS/* fields in their first-cycle degree may be exempted from the interview (a Bachelor final mark of at least 95/110 is also cited as part of the exemption profile) [uncertain]. Non-EU quota: the dedicated public selection for non-European citizens residing abroad reserves a fixed number of places - 10 places in the published 2025/2026 call; the 2026/2027 non-EU call is expected to keep the same order of magnitude [uncertain]. Scoring in the non-EU selection: qualifications (Bachelor's degree, English language, curriculum vitae) are scored first; candidates scoring at least 25/100 are admitted to the interview, candidates below 25 are declared unsuitable; the interview assesses the candidate's personal preparation in Physics for up to 40 points; a final score of at least 50/100 is required to be declared eligible; top-scoring non-EU applicants with at least 90/100 are awarded University of Trento scholarships / tuition fee exemptions. EU/equivalent applicants and non-EU applicants graduating in Italy with a valid residence permit must have completed their Bachelor's degree by 31 October 2026.
language_requirements: English at CEFR level B2 or higher is mandatory for all applicants. Accepted proofs: (a) a language certificate recognised by the University of Trento (standard UniTrento list, e.g. IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge, TOEIC); (b) having passed a university exam certifying English at B2 level as part of the Bachelor's degree programme; (c) an official written statement issued by the home university certifying that the degree programme was taught/delivered in English, or a self-declaration of having graduated in an English-speaking country; (d) for applicants who hold none of the above, passing the English test at the University Language Centre (Centro Linguistico di Ateneo, CLA) before enrolment - written part taken in person in Trento at the CLA, speaking part held online. No Italian language requirement applies for admission, since the whole programme is delivered in English; Italian is only relevant for daily life and optional CLA Italian courses.
application_deadline_eu: Academic year 2026/2027: rolling admission sessions running from June 2026, with the online 'Request for admission' open until 12 November 2026; Bachelor's degree completion and enrolment must be finalised by 31 October 2026 for Europeans/equivalents (and for non-Europeans graduating in Italy with a valid study permit). Exact intermediate session cut-off dates are published in the departmental admission call for 2026/27. [uncertain]
application_deadline_non_eu: Academic year 2026/2027: 4 March 2026 for non-European citizens residing abroad (single early call); the ranking list of admitted candidates and scholarship assignments is published by 25 May 2026. Admitted candidates must then pre-enrol on Universitaly at the Italian diplomatic mission in their country and apply for a study visa; enrolment is completed over the summer and no later than 31 October, with arrival in Trento at the start of September. [uncertain]
required_documents: Non-EU public selection (application submitted online via the UniTrento Apply portal, webapps.unitn.it/Apply): copy of a valid passport showing photo and personal data only; curriculum vitae et studiorum; copy of the Bachelor's degree certificate, or a certificate of enrolment stating the expected graduation date if not yet graduated; copy of the official transcript of academic records listing examinations, results/marks and credits (ECTS or local credits); proof of English at B2 level (certificate, university statement or self-declaration); payment of the application fee of EUR 30.00. EU citizens and equivalents: online 'Request for admission' form; applicants who did not obtain their first-cycle degree at the University of Trento must attach a self-declaration of the examinations taken (with credits and scientific-disciplinary sectors) plus degree certificate/transcript; proof of English B2. Additional documents such as a motivation letter or reference letters are not listed as mandatory in the published call. [uncertain]
entry_exam_or_test: No TOLC and no SAT. Selection is by evaluation of qualifications (Bachelor's degree and marks, curriculum vitae, English proficiency) followed, where required, by an oral interview with a committee appointed by the Department of Physics assessing personal preparation in Physics (worth up to 40 points in the non-EU selection). Interviews for non-EU applicants are conducted remotely (online oral test) after publication of the list of candidates admitted to the oral test. EU/equivalent applicants receive the interview date, time, place and committee composition by e-mail from Student Support; applicants meeting the higher ECTS thresholds (>=30 ECTS MAT/*, >=90 ECTS FIS/*) may be exempted from the interview. A separate English test at the CLA applies only to candidates who cannot otherwise document B2 English.
